views.name: matches_with_card
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Matches.id AS id,
  Matches.card_id AS card_id,
  Matches.winner_id AS winner_id,
  Matches.loser_id AS loser_id,
  Matches.win_type AS win_type,
  Matches.match_type_id AS match_type_id,
  Matches.duration AS duration,
  Matches.title_id AS title_id,
  Matches.title_change AS title_change,
  Cards.table_id AS table_id,
  Cards.location_id AS location_id,
  Cards.promotion_id AS promotion_id,
  Cards.event_date AS event_date,
  Cards.event_id AS event_id,
  Cards.url AS url,
  Tables.html AS html,
  Tables.url AS table_url,
  Locations.name AS name,
  Promotions.name AS name_1,
  Events.name AS name_2
FROM Matches
LEFT JOIN Cards ON Matches.card_id = Cards.id
LEFT JOIN Tables ON Cards.table_id = Tables.id
LEFT JOIN Locations ON Cards.location_id = Locations.id
LEFT JOIN Promotions ON Cards.promotion_id = Promotions.id
LEFT JOIN Events ON Cards.event_id = Events.id
views.description: One row per match with card-level attributes attached (event date, promotion, location, event name, and card source table). Use this when you need match facts contextualized by the card/show they occurred on. | Use for: List matches with their event date and promotion; Filter matches by location or promotion and aggregate outcomes; Join match durations to card-level metadata or source HTML

views.name: matches_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  card_id AS card_id,
  winner_id AS winner_id,
  loser_id AS loser_id,
  win_type AS win_type,
  match_type_id AS match_type_id,
  duration AS duration,
  title_id AS title_id,
  title_change AS title_change
FROM Matches
views.description: One row per match with cleaned/normalized core match columns. Keeps all original identifiers as-is (including textual winner_id/loser_id) so downstream joins to Wrestlers can decide on casting. Good base for match-level filters and aggregations. | Use for: Aggregate match counts by win_type or match_type_id; Filter matches that were title changes; Parse/convert duration values in later processing

views.name: wrestler_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  name AS name
FROM Wrestlers
views.description: One row per wrestler with id and name. Use to join wrestler display names to matches or to deduplicate wrestler references. Keep columns verbatim for straightforward joins. | Use for: Attach wrestler names to matches (winner/loser); Lookup wrestler id by name for filtering or joins

views.name: matches_with_wrestler_names
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.card_id AS card_id,
  m.winner_id AS winner_id,
  w1.name AS name,
  m.loser_id AS loser_id,
  w2.name AS name_1,
  m.win_type AS win_type,
  m.match_type_id AS match_type_id,
  m.duration AS duration,
  m.title_id AS title_id,
  m.title_change AS title_change
FROM Matches AS m
LEFT JOIN Wrestlers AS w1 ON m.winner_id = w1.id
LEFT JOIN Wrestlers AS w2 ON m.loser_id = w2.id
views.description: One row per match with winner and loser names included. Useful for reporting match results in readable form. Note: winner_id/loser_id are stored as TEXT in Matches; this CTE joins on equality which will succeed when ids are numeric and matching types; downstream logic may need casting or cleaning if ids are non-numeric. | Use for: Generate human-readable match lists (Winner vs Loser); Filter matches by wrestler names

views.name: matches_title_changes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  card_id AS card_id,
  winner_id AS winner_id,
  loser_id AS loser_id,
  win_type AS win_type,
  match_type_id AS match_type_id,
  duration AS duration,
  title_id AS title_id,
  title_change AS title_change
FROM Matches
WHERE title_change = 1
views.description: Subset of matches that involved a title change. One row per match where title_change indicates a new champion. Use to analyze title change events across promotions and time. | Use for: List all title changes and link to belt names; Count title changes by promotion or year

views.name: cards_with_location_promotion
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Cards.id AS id,
  Cards.table_id AS table_id,
  Cards.location_id AS location_id,
  Locations.name AS name,
  Cards.promotion_id AS promotion_id,
  Promotions.name AS name_1,
  Cards.event_date AS event_date,
  Cards.event_id AS event_id,
  Cards.url AS url
FROM Cards
LEFT JOIN Locations ON Cards.location_id = Locations.id
LEFT JOIN Promotions ON Cards.promotion_id = Promotions.id
views.description: One row per card with location name and promotion name attached. Useful for card-level summaries by place or promotion. | Use for: Count cards per location or promotion; Map event dates to promotion names
